hints: Particle $P$ is at instantaneous rest at point $X$ when its velocity is zero: $v_P(t) = 0$.
Set $6t - 0.3t^2 = 0$ and solve for the non-zero time $t = 20\text{ s}$.
Integrate velocity with respect to time to obtain displacement $s_P(t) = 3t^2 - 0.1t^3$, then evaluate $s_P(20)$ to find the distance $OX$.
walkthrough:
Find the time $t$ when particle $P$ comes to instantaneous rest at $X$:
$$v_P(t) = 6t - 0.3t^2 = 0 \implies 0.3t(20 - t) = 0 \implies t = 20\text{ s}$$

Integrate velocity from $t = 0$ to $t = 20\text{ s}$ to find distance $OX$:
$$s(t) = \int (6t - 0.3t^2)\,dt = 3t^2 - 0.1t^3$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Particle $P$ starts from $O$ and comes to instantaneous rest at $X$ when its velocity is zero:
$$v(t) = 0$$
$$6t - 0.3t^2 = 0$$
Since $t > 0$, particle $P$ reaches $X$ at time $t = 20\text{ s}$.

Find displacement by integrating velocity with respect to time:
$$s(t) = \int v(t)\,dt = \int (6t - 0.3t^2)\,dt = \frac{6t^2}{2} - \frac{0.3t^3}{3} = 3t^2 - 0.1t^3$$

hints: For particle $Q$, integrate acceleration $a_Q(t) = k - 12t$ to find velocity $v_Q(t) = kt - 6t^2$ (using $v_Q(0) = 0$).
Substitute $t = 10\text{ s}$ and equate the displacement to distance $OX = 400\text{ m}$ to solve for $k$.
walkthrough:
Integrate acceleration $a_Q(t) = k - 12t$ from rest to find velocity $v_Q(t)$:
$$v_Q(t) = \int (k - 12t)\,dt = kt - 6t^2$$

Apply the condition that particle $Q$ reaches $X$ ($s_Q = 400\text{ m}$) at $t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$\frac{1}{2}k(10^2) - 2(10^3) = 400 \implies 50k - 2000 = 400$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Particle $Q$ moves with acceleration $a_Q(t) = k - 12t$. Integrate acceleration to find velocity:
$$v_Q(t) = \int (k - 12t)\,dt = kt - 6t^2 + c_1$$

Since $Q$ starts from rest ($v(0) = 0$), the constant of integration is $c_1 = 0$, giving:
$$v_Q(t) = kt - 6t^2$$

Integrate velocity to find displacement:
$$s_Q(t) = \int (kt - 6t^2)\,dt = \frac{kt^2}{2} - \frac{6t^3}{3} + c_2 = \frac{1}{2}kt^2 - 2t^3 + c_2$$

We are given that particle $Q$ arrives at point $X$ ($s_Q = 400\text{ m}$) when $t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$\frac{1}{2}k(10^2) - 2(10^3) = 400$$
$$\frac{1}{2}k(100) - 2(1000) = 400$$
$$50k - 2000 = 400$$

Add $2000$ to both sides and divide by $50$:
$$50k = 2400$$
$$k = \frac{2400}{50} = 48$$
